provenance.quote: 16:53:49.398 Frequency breaches 48.8Hz trigger level resulting in LFDD. 931MW of demand is automatically disconnected. DNOs
provenance.section: 3.3 Detailed Timeline, Table 1 – Timeline of Events

provenance.quote: The DNO’s have indicated that 931MW (3.2%) of demand was automatically disconnected by the operation of the LFDD scheme.

blocks.response_text: The ESO timeline row attributed to the DNOs reads: at 16:53:49.398 [reported] frequency breached the 48.8 Hz [reported] trigger level, resulting in LFDD, and 931 MW [reported] of demand was automatically disconnected. The DNOs indicated that this was 931 MW (3.2%) [reported] of demand.

provenance.quote: The information is based on DNO reported data as of 13 August 2019 at 12:00.

provenance.section: 5.1 Distribution Demand, Table 6 - DNO customers affected by LFDD relays

blocks.response_text: Our returns as of 13 August 2019 at 12:00 [reported] total 931 MW [reported] and 1,152,878 [reported] customers, with the last area's final restoration at 17:37 [reported].

provenance.quote: Post event, two DNOs reported that a number of LFDD stage 1 schemes did not trigger, and therefore did not disconnect demand.
the system frequency did not stay at 48.8Hz long enough to trigger the operation of all LFDD schemes
the +/-0.01Hz tolerance setting on the LFDD schemes which meant that when the system frequency fell to 48.792Hz, not all schemes were triggered.

blocks.response_text: After the event, two DNOs reported that a number of stage 1 LFDD schemes did not trigger and so did not disconnect demand. The possible reasons given were that the frequency did not stay at 48.8 Hz [reported] long enough to trigger all schemes, or the +/-0.01 Hz [reported] tolerance setting, which meant that when frequency fell to 48.792 Hz [reported] not all schemes triggered.

provenance.quote: SP Distribution erroneously disconnected 22MW of demand in Scotland when the system frequency fell to 48.8Hz. The Grid Code does not require Distribution Network Operators to disconnect demand until the frequency reaches 48.5Hz. The demand disconnection occurred due to an incorrect setting on SP Distribution’s LFDD equipment and has since been corrected.

blocks.response_text: SP Distribution disconnected 22 MW [reported] of demand in Scotland when frequency fell to 48.8 Hz [reported], although the Grid Code does not require DNOs there to disconnect until 48.5 Hz [reported]. It was due to an incorrect setting on its LFDD equipment, which has since been corrected.

provenance.quote: Indications are that DNOs did ask specific permission from the ESO control room to restore demand.
Whilst some DNOs incorrectly called the NGET control room, NGET control room correctly referred DNO’s to the ESO

blocks.response_text: According to the ESO, DNOs asked the ESO control room for specific permission before restoring demand, and some DNOs first called the NGET control room, which referred them to the ESO.

provenance.quote: Eastern Power Networks plc and South Eastern Power Networks plc (both owned by UK Power Networks) reconnected sites without being told to do so by the ESO, and acknowledge that they do not appear to have technically met the requirements of the Grid Code
These instances were caused by the configuration of the DNOs’ operational systems.

blocks.response_text: Ofgem reports that Eastern Power Networks and South Eastern Power Networks, both owned by UK Power Networks, reconnected sites without being told to do so by the ESO and acknowledge that they do not appear to have technically met the Grid Code requirements; Ofgem attributes this to the configuration of their operational systems.

provenance.quote: All DNOs have responded to this request and indicated a combined total of 462MW of embedded generation was lost during the event.

In providing their analysis some DNOs noted challenges in obtaining the data due to the way it is collected or stored and without confirmation from generators, DNOs were unable to determine whether a specific generator tripped due to RoCoF or Vector Shift.

blocks.response_text: All DNOs responded to the ESO's request and together indicated 462 MW [reported] of embedded generation lost during the event. Some of us had trouble obtaining the data because of the way it is collected or stored, and without confirmation from the generators we could not tell whether a given generator tripped on RoCoF or on vector shift.

provenance.quote: Most of the DNOs only record information on generation volumes on their networks on a half-hourly basis, obscuring shorter-term events
as they also do not monitor output from distributed generators in real-time.
provenance.section: Ofgem section 2, Summary of the event, footnote 19

blocks.response_text: Most DNOs record generation volumes on their networks only half-hourly, which obscures short events like this one, and DNOs do not monitor distributed generator output in real time.

provenance.quote: the DNOs have indicated that 4.0% of demand was actually disconnected equating to over 1 million customers

blocks.response_text: To the E3C the DNOs indicated that 4.0% [reported] of demand was actually disconnected, equating to over 1 million [reported] customers.
